description: Haemul Pajeon is a beloved Korean savory pancake, celebrated for its crispy edges and tender interior packed with fresh seafood and vibrant green onions. This classic dish offers a delightful textural contrast and a burst of oceanic flavors, making it a perfect appetizer or light meal. Enjoy this authentic recipe that brings the taste of a bustling Korean market right to your kitchen.

ingredients.notes: shrimp, squid, mussels, clams, cut into bite-sized pieces

instructions.title: Prepare the Dipping Sauce
instructions.text: In a small bowl, whisk together soy sauce, rice vinegar, sugar, sesame oil, toasted sesame seeds, and optional red pepper flakes. Set aside.

instructions.title: Prepare Seafood and Vegetables
instructions.text: If using frozen seafood, thaw and pat dry thoroughly. Cut any larger pieces of seafood into bite-sized portions. Wash and trim green onions, cutting them into 3-inch lengths. Thinly slice the yellow onion and red chili pepper if using.

instructions.title: Make the Batter
instructions.text: In a large bowl, whisk together all-purpose flour, rice flour, salt, and egg. Gradually add the cold water or anchovy broth, whisking until a smooth, lump-free batter forms. The consistency should be slightly thinner than pancake batter.

instructions.title: Combine Ingredients
instructions.text: Add the prepared mixed seafood and sliced yellow onion to the batter. Gently mix to combine, ensuring the seafood and onion are evenly coated. Do not overmix.

instructions.title: Cook the Pancakes
instructions.text: Heat 1-2 tablespoons of vegetable oil in a large non-stick skillet over medium-high heat. Once hot, pour about 1/4 of the batter into the skillet, spreading it evenly to form a round pancake. Arrange about 1/4 of the green onion lengths on top of the batter, pressing them gently into the pancake. Cook for 4-5 minutes until the bottom is golden brown and crispy. Drizzle a little more oil around the edges, then carefully flip the pancake. Cook for another 3-4 minutes until the other side is golden and the seafood is cooked through. Repeat with the remaining batter, green onions, and oil to make 3 more pancakes.

instructions.title: Serve Immediately
instructions.text: Transfer the cooked Haemul Pajeon to a cutting board and slice into wedges. Serve hot with the prepared dipping sauce on the side. Enjoy as an appetizer or a light meal.

tips: For extra crispiness, use a combination of plain flour and rice flour. A splash of sparkling water or ice water in the batter can also help achieve a lighter, crispier texture.

Feel free to customize the seafood mix. Shrimp, squid, mussels, and clams are common, but you can use your favorites or what's available. Ensure all seafood is fresh and cut to a similar size for even cooking.
Serve Haemul Pajeon immediately after cooking for the best texture. If making ahead, reheat in a dry skillet or oven to restore some crispiness, but fresh is always best.
article:
Dive into the heart of Korean comfort food with Haemul Pajeon, a savory seafood pancake that’s as delightful to make as it is to eat. This iconic dish, known for its crispy edges, tender interior, and generous medley of fresh seafood and vibrant green onions, has captivated palates worldwide. Whether you’re a seasoned Korean food enthusiast or new to its incredible flavors, learning to make authentic Haemul Pajeon at home is a rewarding experience that promises to transport your taste buds straight to the bustling streets of Seoul. Get ready to master the art of this beloved Korean pancake, perfect for sharing with friends and family, especially on a cozy evening or a rainy day.

## What is Haemul Pajeon?
Haemul Pajeon (해물파전) literally translates to "seafood green onion pancake." It’s a quintessential Korean savory pancake, a staple in homes, restaurants, and street food stalls across the country. The magic of Haemul Pajeon lies in its harmonious blend of textures and flavors: a slightly chewy, yet often crispy-edged batter, packed with an abundance of tender green onions and a delightful mix of fresh seafood. Common seafood additions include shrimp, squid, mussels, oysters, and clams, though the specific combination can vary.

More than just a dish, Haemul Pajeon holds a special place in Korean culture. It's often associated with rainy days, as the sizzling sound of the pancake frying is said to mimic the sound of falling rain, making it a popular pairing with a bowl of makgeolli (Korean rice wine). Its comforting nature, combined with its vibrant appearance and satisfying taste, makes it a go-to appetizer, side dish, or even a light meal. The balance of earthy green onions with the briny sweetness of seafood, all bound by a light, savory batter, creates an irresistible culinary experience.

## Ingredients for Haemul Pajeon
Crafting the perfect Haemul Pajeon starts with fresh, quality ingredients. Here’s what you’ll need to gather:

For the Batter:
*   1 cup all-purpose flour
*   1/4 cup rice flour (for extra crispiness)
*   1 tablespoon cornstarch (for tenderness)
*   1/2 teaspoon salt
*   1 large egg
*   1 1/2 cups cold water (or cold anchovy broth for deeper flavor)

For the Fillings:
*   6-8 large green onions, trimmed and cut into 3-4 inch lengths (or chopped into 1-inch pieces if preferred)
*   1 cup mixed seafood (e.g., shrimp, squid, mussels, scallops, clams) – fresh or frozen, thawed and thoroughly patted dry. Cut larger pieces into bite-sized chunks.
*   Optional: 1/4 cup thinly sliced onion, 1 red chili pepper (sliced for garnish or a touch of heat)
*   Vegetable oil, for frying

For the Dipping Sauce:
*   3 tablespoons soy sauce
*   1 tablespoon white vinegar
*   1 teaspoon sugar
*   1 teaspoon sesame oil
*   1 teaspoon toasted sesame seeds
*   1/2 teaspoon gochugaru (Korean chili flakes, optional)
*   1 clove garlic, minced
*   1 tablespoon finely chopped green onion

## Step-by-Step Haemul Pajeon Instructions
Follow these steps for a delicious, homemade Haemul Pajeon:

1.  **Prepare the Seafood and Green Onions:** If using frozen seafood, ensure it's fully thawed. Pat all seafood very dry with paper towels to prevent a soggy pancake. Cut shrimp into halves, squid into rings or small squares, and any other larger seafood into bite-sized pieces. Trim the roots off the green onions and cut them into 3-4 inch lengths. If you prefer, you can chop them into 1-inch pieces for easier mixing.
2.  **Make the Batter:** In a large bowl, whisk together the all-purpose flour, rice flour, cornstarch, and salt. In a separate small bowl, whisk the egg with the cold water (or broth). Gradually pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients, whisking until just combined. A few lumps are perfectly fine; do not overmix, as this can develop gluten and make the pancake tough.
3.  **Combine Fillings with Batter:** Gently fold the prepared seafood and most of the green onions into the batter. If you plan to arrange the green onions decoratively on top, reserve about a quarter of them for this step.
4.  **Heat the Pan:** Heat a large (10-12 inch) non-stick skillet or cast-iron pan over medium-high heat. Add a generous amount of vegetable oil (about 2-3 tablespoons) to coat the bottom of the pan. The oil should be shimmering hot.
5.  **Cook the Pancake:** Pour about 1 to 1.5 cups of the batter mixture into the hot pan, spreading it evenly with the back of a ladle to form a thin, round pancake. If you reserved green onions, arrange them nicely on top of the pancake, pressing them gently into the batter. You can also add a few extra pieces of seafood on top for presentation.
6.  **Fry until Golden:** Cook for 3-5 minutes on the first side, until the edges are golden brown and crispy, and the batter appears mostly set. Drizzle a little more oil around the edges of the pancake.
7.  **Flip and Cook Second Side:** Carefully flip the pancake using a large spatula. Cook for another 3-5 minutes on the second side until it's golden brown, crispy, and cooked through. You can press down gently on the pancake with your spatula to ensure even cooking and crispiness.
8.  **Repeat:** Transfer the cooked Haemul Pajeon to a cutting board and repeat the process with the remaining batter, adding more oil to the pan as needed for each pancake.
9.  **Prepare Dipping Sauce:** While the pancakes are cooking, combine all dipping sauce ingredients in a small bowl and mix well.
10. **Serve:** Cut the hot Haemul Pajeon into wedges and serve immediately with the dipping sauce on the side.

## Tips for the Perfect Crispy Haemul Pajeon
Achieving that coveted crispy exterior and tender interior for your Haemul Pajeon requires a few key techniques:

*   **Cold Water is Key:** Using very cold water (or even ice water) for your batter helps to inhibit gluten development, resulting in a lighter, crispier pancake.
*   **Don't Skimp on Rice Flour and Cornstarch:** The combination of all-purpose flour with rice flour and cornstarch is crucial. Rice flour contributes to the distinct crispiness, while cornstarch adds a pleasant tenderness to the batter.
*   **Avoid Overmixing the Batter:** A slightly lumpy batter is better than an overmixed one. Overmixing develops gluten, which can make your pancake tough and chewy rather than tender.
*   **Generous Oil is Your Friend:** Don't be shy with the oil when frying. A good amount of hot oil is essential for achieving those wonderfully golden and crispy edges. Think shallow-frying rather than just pan-frying.
*   **Maintain Medium-High Heat:** Consistent medium-high heat ensures that the pancake crisps up nicely without burning the exterior before the interior is cooked through.
*   **Thin Pancakes are Crispier:** Spread your batter thinly in the pan. Thicker pancakes tend to be softer and less crispy.
*   **Pat Seafood Dry:** Excess moisture from the seafood can make your pancake soggy. Always pat your seafood thoroughly dry with paper towels before adding it to the batter.

## Serving Suggestions & Dipping Sauce
Haemul Pajeon is best enjoyed fresh off the pan, while it's still warm and crispy. Cut it into wedges or squares for easy sharing.

The classic dipping sauce for Haemul Pajeon is simple yet adds a burst of tangy, savory, and slightly spicy flavor that perfectly complements the pancake. To make it:
Combine 3 tablespoons soy sauce, 1 tablespoon white vinegar, 1 teaspoon sugar, 1 teaspoon sesame oil, 1 teaspoon toasted sesame seeds, 1/2 teaspoon gochugaru (Korean chili flakes, if desired), 1 minced clove of garlic, and 1 tablespoon finely chopped green onion. Stir well until the sugar dissolves.

Haemul Pajeon pairs wonderfully with a variety of Korean beverages. As mentioned, it's traditionally enjoyed with makgeolli, especially on a rainy day, for a truly authentic experience. It also goes great with soju or a cold beer. Beyond drinks, it makes an excellent appetizer for any Korean meal, a satisfying snack, or even a light lunch or dinner when you’re craving something warm and savory.

## Haemul Pajeon Variations
While the classic Haemul Pajeon is a masterpiece, the "jeon" (pancake) concept in Korean cuisine is incredibly versatile, allowing for numerous delicious variations based on the same basic batter principle:

*   **Kimchi Pajeon (Kimchijeon):** For those who love a bit of a kick, add chopped, well-fermented kimchi to your batter. The sourness and spice of kimchi create a vibrant and addictive pancake. You can still add seafood, or make it vegetarian.
*   **Buchujeon (Garlic Chive Pancake):** Replace green onions entirely with fresh garlic chives for a distinct, aromatic flavor. This version is often lighter and less dense, with a strong, fresh chive taste.
*   **Hobakjeon (Zucchini Pancake):** Thinly sliced zucchini can be incorporated into the batter or simply pan-fried in a similar style. It offers a milder, sweeter flavor.
*   **Meat Pajeon:** Instead of seafood, thinly sliced beef (bulgogi-style) or pork can be added to the batter for a heartier, meaty pancake.
*   **Vegetable Pajeon:** Create a purely vegetarian version by filling your pancake with a colorful array of vegetables such as sliced carrots, onions, mushrooms, bell peppers, and zucchini. This is a great way to use up leftover vegetables.
*   **Mushroom Pajeon:** Focus on various types of mushrooms (shiitake, oyster, enoki) for an earthy and umami-rich pancake.

The beauty of these variations is that the fundamental batter recipe remains largely the same, making it easy to experiment and find your favorite combination.

Mastering Haemul Pajeon is not just about following a recipe; it's about embracing a piece of Korean culinary culture. With its delightful crunch, fresh seafood, and savory green onions, this pancake is sure to become a cherished dish in your cooking repertoire. So gather your ingredients, fire up your skillet, and get ready to enjoy the incredible flavors of homemade Haemul Pajeon – a true Korean comfort food classic.
